messages:
sam: heads-up — multi-node TP job (8 nodes) stalled at step 1024. ranks are up but collective ops appear to be requeueing, not an OOM.
maria: can you paste the short trace/console lines?
sam: snippet from node logs:
```
[0] NCCL INFO op 1024 allreduce queued -> issued
[0] NCCL WARN op 1024 timeout wait 5000ms
[3] NCCL INFO rank3 op 1024 completed
[7] NCCL INFO rank7 stuck in reduce_scatter
```
jin: odd. perf profiler from the same run shows big kernel selection divergence across ranks — some ranks hit an optimized fused kernel, others fall back to a generic matmul.
sam: exact excerpt from perf (aggregated):
```
rank0: fused_matmul_v2 48.2% | allreduce 12.5% | memcpy 8.7%
rank1: fallback_matmul   62.1% | allreduce 2.3%  | memcpy 14.0%
rank4: fused_matmul_v2 45.0% | allreduce 10.2% | memcpy 9.8%
rank5: fallback_matmul   59.9% | allreduce 3.0%  | memcpy 13.1%
```
maria: that explains staggered collectives — if compute runtimes diverge per-rank, NCCL schedules get out of phase and ops linger.
kai: any idea why kernel selector picked different paths? same model artifact on all nodes?
sam: same model, same build. suspect is KV cache behavior + recent kvcache heuristic change landed yesterday which evicts aggressively under slight mem pressure.
jin: if a rank evicts prefixes earlier it changes the shape/seq distribution observed by the kernel selector at runtime -> different code path chosen -> imbalance.
maria: can you repro locally with a smaller cluster?
sam: yes, repro with 4-node mini. commands we used to reproduce:
```
REDWOOD_KV_EVICT=1 KERNEL_SELECTOR_DBG=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO \
  ./run_inference --nodes 4 --tp 8 --seq 2048 --batch 1
```
kai: quick mitigation that unblocked our staging run: force the optimized kernel on all ranks:
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=fused_matmul_v2 ./run_inference --nodes 8 ...
```
sam: that works as a short-term workaround but not ideal.
maria: proposed immediate actions:
- revert the kvcache eviction heuristic patch (regression likely cause)
- add a rendezvous-time kernel-selection parity check (fail fast if ranks pick different kernels)
- add TP perf test CI that asserts per-rank kernel parity for identical workloads
jin: also add better tracing: emit kernel-id in NCCL debug spans and surface collective latency per-rank so we detect divergence before a full stall.
infra-bot: Incident INC-3557 created: "tp multi-node kernel-path skew -> lingering NCCL ops". Assignees: eng-runtime (sam, jin, maria).
maria: I'm opening the revert PR now and attaching the perf traces, ETA EOD for the revert + test. will also add a followup to sync kernel selector decisions at rendezvous.
sam: thanks — if you hit this in the meantime, use REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE as a mitigation and include your perf snippet when filing.
jin: adding a note: we should also audit batching heuristics because kvcache eviction + microbatch scheduling interaction could amplify per-rank shape differences.
kai: agreed — will start a small perf sweep across seq lengths 512/1024/2048 to map sensitivity.
maria: ok locking in that plan. :thumbsup:
